terms.gloss: a property, an estate, in town or country
evidence: Cato Agr. 1.1: praedium quom parāre cōgitābis
Cic. Rosc. Com. 33: cum jacērent pretia praediōrum, when property prices were low
terms.comment: Land or buildings owned: praedium urbānum, a building in town (Cic. Verr. 2.3.199, Lewis & Short); praedium rūsticum, land in the country (Nep. Att. 14.3).

evidence: Nep. Att. 14.3: in Ēpīrōticīs et urbānīs possessiōnibus
Cic. Rosc. Com. 33: omnium possessiōnēs erant incertae

terms.gloss: a farm, a piece of land
dealer in landed property; Traupman: real-estate broker
terms.comment: Classically one who bought estates sold at auction for debt (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: praedium quom parāre cōgitābis, sīc in animō habētō: utī nē cupidē emās nēve operā tuā parcās vīsere et nē satis habeās semel circumīre
phrases.english: when you are thinking of buying a property, keep this in mind: don’t buy in a hurry, don’t spare yourself the trouble of going to see it, and don’t think it enough to walk round it once

phrases.latin: Accēpit enim agrum temporibus eīs cum jacērent pretia praediōrum
phrases.english: for he took over the land at a time when property prices were low

sources: Lewis & Short: praedium · Lewis & Short: possessio · Lewis & Short: fundus · Lewis & Short: praediator
